one_liner: Discord has a broad, free REST API with OAuth2 for users and bot tokens, self-serve via the Developer Portal; only community MCP servers exist.
auth_notes: Authorization-code OAuth2 with self-serve app registration covers user-scoped endpoints. Bot tokens handle most guild operations and are static secrets. Basic auth (client_id:client_secret) applies only to token endpoints. Some scopes are partner-only.
access_notes: Anyone can register a developer application and get a client ID, secret and bot token for free. Privileged intents need review only above 10,000 users.
blocker_notes: Privileged intent review applies only past 10,000 users, which does not affect building or testing. Some scopes are partner-only.

evidence.quote: We support the authorization code grant, the implicit grant, client credentials, and some modified special-for-Discord flows for Bots and Webhooks.
Using a bot token found on the Bot page within your app’s settings.
Both are free; automating a personal account is forbidden.
Apps with server-installed user counts fewer than 10,000 can toggle privileged intents in the Developer Portal.
You can use the [Discord OpenAPI Spec](https://github.com/discord/discord-api-spec) to generate a client in your preferred backend language
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides Discord integration capabilities to MCP clients like Claude Desktop.
